summary: scripts/backfill-cost.ts: compute cost_usd for existing queries rows from model_pricing; one-shot operator script
description:
scripts/backfill-cost.ts — one-shot operator script for existing queries rows.

Live data so far: 9 OpenRouter requests, ~$0.167 total (DeepSeek 7 / Sonnet 2). All have model_used, input_tokens, output_tokens, but cost_usd will be NULL after child 1's migration.

Algorithm:
  SELECT id, model_used, input_tokens, output_tokens, created_at
  FROM queries
  WHERE cost_usd IS NULL
    AND model_used IS NOT NULL
    AND input_tokens IS NOT NULL
    AND output_tokens IS NOT NULL;

For each row: cost_usd = computeCost({ modelId: model_used, inputTokens, outputTokens, cachedInputTokens: 0, at: created_at }).  Update the row.

Limitation: cached_input_tokens isn't recoverable for historical rows (we never logged it).  Backfill uses 0 for the cached-token count, so backfilled cost slightly over-estimates true cost for cache-using historical Sonnet calls.  Acceptable for the current 2 Sonnet rows (both pre-tier-pro, no cache hits expected).

After backfill:
- SUM(cost_usd) FROM queries should be within $0.01 of OpenRouter's reported $0.167.
- Post any remaining diff to ops chat / log it; spec is 'never recompute cost', so no second-pass adjustment.

Done when:
- ts script that runs via 'tsx scripts/backfill-cost.ts' (or 'npm run backfill-cost')
- Idempotent: cost_usd IS NOT NULL rows are skipped on re-run
- Documented: README routine for 'after deploying child 5, run this once on prod'
- Manual: SUM(cost_usd) ≈ OpenRouter reported total
